Chapter 10: Living with Openness and Joy
As the journey unfolds, something unexpected starts to happen. Sure, the struggles and discomfort haven’t disappeared, but now, they’re joined by moments of ease, gratitude, and even—yes—real joy. Life, with all its messiness, just feels a little lighter.
Picture this. One morning, someone wakes up to the sound of birds outside their window. Instead of rushing headlong into the day’s worries, they pause. They just listen. It’s such a simple moment, but it brings a smile. And for a few seconds, everything feels just right.
Most of us spend so much time zeroed in on what’s wrong, or what needs to change, that we miss the tiny joys waiting right here, right now. The practice of presence isn’t only about facing pain—it’s about opening up to the goodness that’s already around us.
Think back to a time when life felt overwhelming. Maybe work and family demands left you feeling like everything was slipping by. But after months of practicing mindfulness and self-compassion, something changes. You begin to notice the little pleasures—a warm cup of tea, a kind word from a friend, the sunlight warming your face. Sure, these moments don’t erase the hard stuff, but they bring a sense of balance and perspective.
Openness is about being willing to experience life as it is. It’s not about clinging to pleasure, or pushing away pain. It’s saying yes to each moment, trusting that whatever comes your way can be met with presence and kindness.
And joy? It’s not something you chase or try to achieve. Joy emerges naturally when your heart is open and your mind is clear. You’ll find it in the ordinary, the unexpected, and those little moments of connection you share with others.
Over time, living with openness and joy becomes just that—a way of life. The ups and downs are still there, but now they’re held with more ease. The journey stops being about fixing or escaping. Instead, it’s about living fully—embracing all of life, with its beauty and its imperfection.
